reason: Connect the retort to hydrogen to prepare it for processing the iron-rich feedstock.
expectation: I expect the retort to receive a controlled hydrogen supply, though it may need further setup before reduction.

alternatives.reason: The cable and steel may make useful equipment, but the retort connection seems more directly related to making iron.

effect: The retort now has a regulated hydrogen supply; it still needs heat and feedstock.
reaction: The contained exhaust and condensate make the setup feel carefully considered.
reason: Place the retort in the solar heating bay to prepare it for the reduction process.
expectation: I expect the retort to be positioned for solar heating, with further preparation needed before making iron.

alternatives.reason: The cable and steel may be useful later, but heating the retort seems more directly relevant now.

effect: The retort is positioned for heating, but no feedstock action is offered yet.
reaction: The placement is straightforward, though its next use is not yet clear.
reason: The cable and steel combination is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect it to make some powered workshop equipment, but I don't know what.

effect: The cable and steel made a magnetic separator, suggesting the iron-rich fraction must be separated before it enters the retort.
reaction: The switchable magnet gives the otherwise unclear combination a practical purpose.
reason: Use the separator on the screened regolith to prepare the iron-rich feedstock; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect it to collect magnetic grains from the regolith for processing, though they may need further preparation.

effect: The separator produced an assayed iron-rich concentrate ready for the retort.
reaction: The distinction between magnetic minerals and red colour is a useful detail.
reason: Process the concentrate in the hydrogen-fed retort at the heating bay to make iron.
expectation: I expect heating with hydrogen to reduce the iron-bearing minerals, perhaps producing iron that needs further processing.

effect: Hydrogen reduction produced porous iron that needs further forming at the press.
reaction: The explanation of oxygen removal and the weak sponge makes the processing sequence clearer.
reason: Press the reduced iron sponge; it is the only offered gameplay action and should make the metal more usable.
expectation: I expect the press to compact the porous iron, though it may need further treatment.

effect: The heated press cycle consolidated the sponge into a dense billet, completing the iron-making goal; the billet still needs shaping into a frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating metal and shaping parts makes the sequence clearer.
reason: Use the press to shape the consolidated iron for the new process-frame goal; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the press to form the billet into frame components, though assembly may still be needed.

effect: The billet is now shaped into non-pressure supports ready for the process frame.
reaction: The distinction from flight hardware makes their intended use clear.
reason: Fit the bars and brackets to the return-plant footing to build the frame; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect a support frame on the footing, though it may need additional components.

effect: The bars and brackets became a frame on the footing, completing the chapter's final goal.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the locally made iron become a practical support for the gas installation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reducing the concentrate and consolidating the porous iron made the progression from mineral to usable metal clear and physically grounded.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the retort was a necessary but uneventful preparation, and its next use was not yet clear.

surprise.text: The cable and steel made a switchable electromagnet for separating suitable minerals; I hadn't known what that combination would produce.

arbitrary.text: The cable-and-steel pairing lacked a clear purpose before its result, although the electromagnet's role made sense afterward.

continue.text: Yes. The iron-making sequence was informative, and I'd be curious to see how the gas installation and the preserved core fit into the return plan.
